note: THE ENCODED-REF v1 DEPLOY CONTRACT. Frozen. Do not edit to make a test pass.
vlab mints these strings (adopt/adopt/ref_encoding.py); the replybot tag
named by fly's devops/values/production.yaml decodes them
this file exist, one per repo, so neither repo needs the other checked
separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False). Both repos recompute it AND
compare it to a constant hardcoded in their test, so the file cannot be
edited quietly on either side: changing a vector without the digest
fails the self-check, and changing both fails the constant.
A format change is a NEW version, not an edit. Bump ENCODED_REF_VERSION
in both repos and add a v2 fixture beside this one; every ad already
live was published against exactly these bytes.

mint.why: the ordinary case: an 8-byte shortcode and a 5-byte token
the shortest legal shortcode; length prefix 1
multi-byte UTF-8: the prefix counts BYTES (5), not characters (4)
hyphen, underscore and mixed case all survive the shortcode
a 19-byte shortcode, the longest in production use
a 1-byte token: the remainder rule at its minimum
a 10-byte token: the remainder carries no length of its own
high bytes and NULs survive the hex round trip in both directions
the longest shortcode a single length byte can describe
a shortcode with no ASCII in it at all
a token exactly as mint_ref_token produces it, so the fixture pins the minting too and not only the packing

reject.why: a dot: outside base64url, and the separator of the OTHER ref grammar
padding: the wire format is unpadded, and Node re-encodes without it

a lone trailing character: a length no base64 encoder can produce. Node's decoder is LENIENT here and returns a short buffer rather than failing, so this vector is what proves the round-trip check is present
two bytes: shorter than version + length + shortcode + token
version byte 2: a v1 decoder must refuse a future format rather than guess at its layout
a length prefix of 200 with 13 bytes to read: the prefix must be checked against the buffer, never trusted
a whole shortcode and NO token: the remainder must be at least one byte
a shortcode of one space: legal bytes, unusable as a route, and guessing would put a respondent in an arbitrary survey

whatsapp_entry_accept.why: the encoded anchor, exactly as whatsapp_ref emits it
the body is trimmed before matching; a respondent's compose box can carry whitespace
the optional `start ` prefix applies to the encoded anchor too
the dotted anchor still routes, and carries NO token -- which is what `tokenless` means downstream, not a failure
form-first with trailing pairs: what whatsapp_autofill emits in metadata mode
**form. NEED NOT LEAD on the deployed gate.** This is the vector adopt's vendored copy of the pattern rejected on 2026-08-26 -- the drift this fixture exists to make visible
an author-injected `vt` pair is STRIPPED. fly owns `vt` and deletes it unconditionally before the decode branch; without this the ref's author would choose the join key vlab attributes by

whatsapp_entry_reject.why: the encoded anchor is full-match: a dot after the payload means it is not an encoded ref, and the dotted pattern does not match it either

whatsapp_entry_reject.body: hello I would like to join
whatsapp_entry_reject.why: ordinary text. The gate is anchored and full-match precisely so a mid-survey free-text answer cannot re-trigger entry

whatsapp_entry_throws.why: passes the gate's alphabet, fails the decode. getMetadata lets RefDecodeError escape DELIBERATELY -- the encoded ref is the only carrier of the shortcode, so swallowing it would route the respondent into FALLBACK_FORM, silently
